body:
**120 books**, overwhelmingly non-fiction with heavy emphasis on politics, history, recent events, and power structures.

This reading list is a direct window into political and intellectual dimensions of the self model.

The author-level spread is not range. [[wiki/interests/favorites/eclecticism]] originally co-authored that reading; the 2026-09-01 rewrite retires it. Forty of 120 books are tagged `trump` or `jan-6` (thirty authors); twenty are tagged `roman-republic`, `ancient-history` or `caesar` (fourteen authors); the two sets do not overlap. One account per witness is all exhaustive coverage of a single event requires, which is why 85 of 98 authors appear once.

## Dimensions

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total | 120 |
| Unique authors | 98 |
| My Rating 5 | 29 |
| My Rating 4 | 42 |
| My Rating 3 | 32 |
| My Rating 2 | 7 |
| My Rating 1 | 1 |
| My Rating 0 | 9 |
| High-rated (4+) | 71 |

All 120 books carry ratings (unlike music). 5-star examples include Hardcore History (Carlin), Nuclear War (Jacobsen), American Prometheus (Bird), Rubicon (Holland), Caesar (Goldsworthy), The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich (Shirer).

## 2025 update (fresher Goodreads export)

A second, more recent Goodreads export (`raw/self/google-drive-export/goodreads_library_export.md`, 103 rows, 63 marked "read") extends the record into mid-2025 and adds one notable cross-link the master list didn't carry.

Most recent reads by date: *The Price of Justice* (Leamer, Jan 20 2025, ★★★★) → *All or Nothing: How Trump Recaptured America* (Wolff, May 20 2025, ★★★★) → *Shocking Psychological Studies and the Lessons They Teach* (Polk, May 20 2025, ★★★) → *The Politics of Fear* (Goldwag, May 20 2025, ★★★) → *Abundance* (Klein, Jul 16 2025, ★★★ — re-logged; also appears "to-read" elsewhere in the same export, likely a re-read or duplicate entry). The Wolff read means all four of his Trump-era books plus this fifth (2025) volume have now been read — a complete-series read of one author, consistent with the existing Top Authors table.

**Cross-link:** [[wiki/people/jacob-bacharach]] appears in the export exactly once — *The Doorposts of Your House and on Your Gates* (Liveright, **2017**; shelved 2022-03-24, tagged "fiction, 2022"), rated the maximum ★★★★★.

> **CORRECTED [2026-08-08]:** This paragraph previously read "Two of his books read and both top-rated," dated the novel to 2022, and treated *The Bend of the World* as a second five-star entry. Neither the Goodreads export nor `FAVS MASTERLIST.csv` contains *The Bend of the World* at all — 2022 is the shelving date, not the publication year, and only one Bacharach title has ever been logged. This matters beyond the count: *The Bend of the World* is the novel Dan names as the site of the [[wiki/places/155-virginia-ave]] coincidence chain, and the one book of Bacharach's he demonstrably read is the other one — which Bacharach himself identified in February 2021 as the Uniontown novel. The open contradiction is documented on [[wiki/people/jacob-bacharach]].

Also newly visible: *None of This Rocks* (Joe Trohman of Fall Out Boy, memoir, ★☆☆☆☆ — the corpus's only 1-star rating, read Feb 2023) and *Hummingbird: Essays* (Jude Angelini, ★★★★★, memoir/personality) — both worth a look from [[wiki/interests/music]] if a fuller pass is ever done on the memoir/personality cluster.

## Patterns

Strong focus on American political history, journalism, power analysis, and recent events (Trump era, elections, institutions). Ancient/Roman history and war provide broader context. "jan-6", "conspiracy", "leftist", "conservative" tags show engaged skepticism.

Aligns with democratic socialist politics, institutional skepticism, and forensic approach to narratives in [[wiki/self/context-core]].

High volume of "top-shelf" and non-fiction indicates deliberate, serious reading.

## Relation to Self

Reading as extension of political engagement and truth-seeking. Complements Twitter activity and other media consumption. Ties to [[wiki/self/facebook]] political likes (AOC, Trump White House, Dawkins, philosophy, science skepticism) and ads interests.

See [[wiki/self/context-core]] §7 Political + Intellectual and [[wiki/self/overview]].

plain.title: Book Favorites
plain.body:
**The short version.** Dan has rated 120 books across 98 different authors. On its face that looks like impressive breadth. Count the books by subject instead of by author, and the reading list collapses into two obsessions carried by forty-four hands: the last decade of American politics, and the last century of the Roman Republic. The 98-author spread isn't a measure of range. It's what monomania looks like when it reads everything available on a single subject.

## The numbers

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total books | 120 |
| Unique authors | 98 |
| High-rated (4+ stars) | 71 |
| Non-fiction | 106 of 120 |
| Published in 2024 or later | 58 |

All 120 carry ratings — unlike his music list, where many favorites have no score.

## The subjects, counted

| Topic | Books |
|-------|-------|
| Politics | 79 |
| History | 69 |
| 2024 | 58 |
| Recent-history | 55 |
| Trump | 40 |
| President | 35 |
| Journalism | 31 |
| War | 18 |
| January 6 | 18 |
| Roman Republic | 16 |

## The two subjects, counted by author

The contradiction changes how to read the 98-author figure.

- **Forty books tagged `trump` or `jan-6`, by thirty authors** — the four-year degradation of a constitutional order, reconstructed from every available vantage point. *Fire and Fury*, *Siege*, *Landslide*, *Betrayal*, *The Divider*, *Confidence Man*.
- **Twenty books tagged `roman-republic`, `ancient-history`, or `caesar`, by fourteen authors** — the last generation of a different constitutional order. *Death Throes of the Republic*, *Rubicon*, *The Assassination of Julius Caesar*.

The two sets do not overlap. Exactly half the collection is two subjects read through forty-four different hands. Eighty-five of the 98 authors appear exactly once — 86.7% — because one account per witness is all that exhaustive coverage of a single event requires. The author-level spread is produced by subject-level monomania, not by breadth.

## The top authors

| Author | Books |
|--------|-------|
| Bob Woodward | 5 |
| Michael Wolff | 5 |
| Adrian Goldsworthy | 4 |
| Jonathan Karl | 3 |
| Dan Carlin | 2 |
| William L. Shirer | 2 |
| James L. Swanson | 2 |
| Bernie Sanders | 2 |
| Karl Marx | 2 |

Wolff and Karl are the only authors with multiple 5-star ratings (3 and 2 respectively).

## Five-star examples

*Caesar: Life of a Colossus* (Goldsworthy), *Rubicon* (Holland), *The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich* (Shirer), *American Prometheus: The Triumph and Tragedy of J. Robert Oppenheimer* (Bird), *Nuclear War: A Scenario* (Jacobsen), *Hardcore History* (Carlin).

## Reading intensity

Dates cluster heavily in 2024: fifty-three read, fifty-nine added. The political reading surge aligns with the same year Dan was doing his most intensive forensic work on the Trump era and the Capitol. A fresher Goodreads export extends into mid-2025: the most recent reads include a complete-series run through all five of Michael Wolff's Trump-era books, *The Price of Justice*, and *Abundance*.

## The want-to-read queue

149 unread titles. Same obsessions — Rome, Trump-era politics, intelligence and conspiracy history — plus a distinct New York City history thread. *How Democracies Die*, *The Gulag Archipelago*, *The Jakarta Method*, *The Power Broker*, *The Assassination of Fred Hampton*, *The Trial of the Chicago 7*, five separate books on 9/11.

Not one title on that queue is about something being built and working.
